transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO - Northstar), Aisha Khan (Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng)

Summary: Quick model catalog walkthrough focused on selecting open models for Northstar's clinical summarization use case, discussing benchmarks (latency/cost/quality), compatibility matrix for private/dedicated deployments, and next steps for a short POC.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm jordan lee from redwood, i'll kick us off. 
00:08 Carlos Mendes: yeah thanks jordan, appreciate it. we wanted to see how your model catalog maps to our latency and privacy needs before we commit to a POC.
00:18 Jordan Lee: totally, totally. joining me is priya nair, she's our solutions engineer and will do a deeper walkthrough of the console and the compatibility matrix.
00:25 Priya Nair: hi all, hey carlos, aisha, ravi, nice to meet you. i'll show the catalog, how benchmarking works and the matrix that maps models to hardware/quantization options.
00:38 Aisha Khan: quick context: we're building clinical note summarization, throughput about 80 reqs/minute, p95 latency target is sub-600ms per response for short notes, and data can't leave our VPC for PHI.
00:56 Jordan Lee: great, that's helpful. so two immediate cross cuts: privacy (private/dedicated) and latency/cost tradeoff. redwood supports hosted but for PHI we usually recommend dedicated or private deployment.
01:10 Ravi Patel: yeah we need VPC + KMS integrated, also audit logs for compliance. are those in the compatibility docs?
01:20 Priya Nair: yep, the compatibility matrix has columns for deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), KMS support, SOC2, audit log retention, and typical GPU compatibility (A10, A100, H100, etc). i'll pull it up now.
01:36 Priya Nair: (screen) ok on the left is the model catalog, you can filter by task — summarization, chat, embeddings — and by size/latency profile. we surface redwood-verified throughput numbers from our benchmark harness.
01:50 Jordan Lee: quick callout: for open models we often present a few curated picks — small, medium, large — with measured p50/p95 latencies on a few hardware profiles. the goal is to show where quantization helps without regressing quality.
02:06 Aisha Khan: can you give an example for a model we might consider for summarization?
02:11 Priya Nair: sure. for example the 'orca-mini' family (placeholder name) is good for cost-sensitive use cases; we show its latency on 80-token outputs, and also a quality benchmark vs a tuned 7B model. then we also show 'med-llm-7b-q' which is quantized and optimized for H100 with good recall on clinical entities.
02:33 Carlos Mendes: are those tradeoffs baked into the console so we can run our own subset? or do we need a SE to run custom benchmarks?
02:41 Priya Nair: you can run quick comparisons in the console — we have a lightweight benchmark runner for smoke tests; for production-like POCs we typically run a dedicated benchmark with priya/SE assistance so we can tune batch size, KV cache, and quantization profiles.
02:58 Jordan Lee: also note smart routing: if you pick a hosted fallback, we can route lower priority or non-PHI traffic to hosted with the private deployment for PHI, but you said PHI can't leave your VPC so likely dedicated/private only.
03:18 Ravi Patel: yep, we can't send PHI out. so what's required for private deployment? network requirements, image sizes, install steps?
03:25 Priya Nair: private deployment options include a customer-managed control plane with on-prem or VPC installers. requirements are in the matrix link — generally we need a node pool with GPU(s), access to KMS endpoints, and a reading service account. we can share the runbook.
03:45 Aisha Khan: regarding quality, how do you measure regression when we move to quantized variants? we care about entity retention in summaries.
03:53 Priya Nair: we recommend a small eval set of labeled prompts. our 'Optimize' product runs quality monitoring and regression alerts against your prompt set. for the POC we can run both float and quantized profiles and produce a side-by-side diff report.
04:11 Carlos Mendes: pricing — is there a rough delta between float and quantized in terms of $/1k tokens?
04:17 Jordan Lee: roughly quantized runs 30-50% cheaper depending on the model and batching. we'll send a price matrix but benchmarking will give you a more accurate estimate for your workload.
04:28 Ravi Patel: on hardware, do you support multi-GPU KV-cache across requests or is that a future thing?
04:33 Priya Nair: multi-GPU for long-context KV sharing is supported in our dedicated runtime; the compatibility matrix shows which models have efficient sharding support. for short notes, single-GPU with batching is usually efficient.
04:49 Aisha Khan: any compatibility issues with our inference library? we're currently using Triton for some endpoints and a custom wrapper.
04:56 Priya Nair: we can export model artifacts in ONNX/TorchScript and provide a small adapter. many customers use our runtime directly, but we provide integration docs for Triton and KFServing.
05:08 Carlos Mendes: you mentioned benchmark numbers in the catalog — how reliable are they? what's the variance?
05:15 Priya Nair: numbers are from our harness, typical variance +/- 8-12% depending on the workload. for your POC we run the harness with your dataset to reduce variance and tune batch sizes and tokenization.
05:30 Jordan Lee: i'll put a note to include the raw benchmark logs and a template for your infra team to reproduce locally.
05:36 Priya Nair: (screen) here's the compatibility matrix — columns for model, size, quantization flavors (4-bit, 8-bit), recommended hardware, expected p50/p95 for 80-token outputs, and known regressions.
05:52 Aisha Khan: do you have examples of med-specific open models? we saw some names but hard to parse which are fine-tuned on clinical data.
06:00 Priya Nair: we list model provenance; many open models are base models — if you need med-tuning we can recommend providers or run an internal fine-tune as part of the POC. we also show evaluation scores on clinical datasets (de-id, entity F1).
06:21 Carlos Mendes: for security review we'll need SOC2 docs, data residency statements, and KMS integration detail. also SSO/SAML for console access.
06:30 Jordan Lee: yep, we'll share SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported in the console — the compatibility sheet notes which features are in hosted vs private.
06:41 Ravi Patel: can you capture the network requirements in a single file? our infra team will need the CIDR/IPs and ports.
06:47 Priya Nair: yes, runbook + network diagram link will be shared.
06:52 Jordan Lee: let's talk benchmarks — priya, maybe demo the console benchmark runner with a small sample?
06:57 Priya Nair: sure, i'll run a quick 'smoke' benchmark comparing three models: orca-mini-7b, med-llm-7b-q, and a tuned 7b baseline. this will be a short 2-minute run so numbers are crude but illustrative.
07:12 Priya Nair: (typing) launching smoke run... alright initial p50s show: orca-mini p50 ~120ms on A10, med-llm-7b-q p50 ~180ms on A100 quantized, tuned7b p50 ~240ms on A100 float — p95s scale accordingly.
07:34 Aisha Khan: those look promising for latency. how about token costs?
07:38 Jordan Lee: token cost depends on sequence length and batching. we'll attach a cost estimator sheet; in our POC we log token counts to give you $/1000 estimate.
07:48 Carlos Mendes: curious about inference consistency — if we roll out a quantized model and we see a drop in entity F1, do you have rollback/rollout policies?
07:58 Priya Nair: yes, the console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automated rollback on quality regressions defined by your eval set. it's part of our 'Rollouts' feature.
08:12 Ravi Patel: network egress for hosted backups — if we snapshot model logs, where do they go?
08:18 Jordan Lee: for private deployments logs stay in your storage; for hosted we can configure retention and region. we'll note that for PHI use cases you should keep logs in your VPC.
08:27 Aisha Khan: great. can we talk about quantization flavors — what do you support? 4-bit, 8-bit, mixed? any caveats?
08:35 Priya Nair: we support 8-bit and some 4-bit profiles. caveat is some 4-bit kernels are newer and might change numeric behaviour slightly; we recommend running regressions on your eval prompts. the compatibility matrix flags models with production-ready 4-bit kernels.
08:53 Carlos Mendes: do you have a compatibility mapping for our planned infra? we're on GCP (vertex) and also have an on-prem cluster with A10s.
08:59 Priya Nair: yes, the sheet has a column for cloud compatibility; for Vertex we recommend certain images and runtime flags. on-prem A10s are fine for small-medium loads; H100/A100 recommended for high throughput.
09:13 Jordan Lee: i'll highlight the recommended target for your 80 reqs/min profile in the notes we send.
09:19 Priya Nair: ok i'm bookmarking the models in the console and attaching the quick smoke results to the meeting notes.
09:26 Carlos Mendes: next steps from our side: we can provide a 1k-sample dataset and some labeled examples for entity F1 by the end of the week.
09:34 Aisha Khan: and we'll identify success criteria — minimum entity F1 and latency SLA.
09:40 Jordan Lee: perfect. to recap, we'll send model catalog deck, compatibility matrix, SOC2 docs, benchmark template; priya will run a POC benchmark once you provide the dataset. target POC kickoff week of 4/6.
09:56 Carlos Mendes: sounds good. thanks all.
10:00 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed POC plan.

Notes on transcript quality: Some names and model names may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "orca-mini" may be recorded differently). Shared artifacts: Model catalog deck (link), compatibility matrix (link to spreadsheet), benchmark template (link).

End of transcript.
